$comment: DOCUMENTED EXCEPTIONS TO THE npm-audit HIGH/CRITICAL GATE.
⚠️ THIS IS EXCEPTION-WITH-DEBT, NOT AN OVERRIDE. The standing rule is that a
gate override requires an immediate debt-payment task; 'precedent' was
retired on 2026-07-23 after the auth/babel bump. So every entry here MUST
carry a retirement condition naming the work that removes it, and the gate
refuses an entry that does not.
⚠️ KEYED BY ADVISORY ID, NEVER BY PACKAGE NAME. An exception for a package
would silently absorb the NEXT advisory published against it — which is the
one nobody has read. A new id fails the gate even on an excepted package.
⚠️ AND A STALE ENTRY FAILS THE GATE TOO. An exception that no longer matches
any advisory is a justification nobody has re-read, sitting where a reader
will take it for a live decision. Prose decays silently; the gate does not
let it. Delete the entry when the advisory is gone.

exceptions.justification: This is a POSTGRES application and the driver never loads. MEASURED, not asserted: packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma declares provider = "postgresql"; no file under apps/*/src or packages/*/src imports mysql2 or mysql; and mysql2 is declared by node_modules/prisma — the CLI — which is a devDependency in every package.json that names it (root, apps/meddoc-pro, packages/db). The SHIPPED runtime is @prisma/client, which this advisory is not about. The advisory describes an auth-plugin downgrade leaking plaintext credentials to a MySQL server; there is no MySQL server, no MySQL connection string, and no code path that constructs one. prisma is nonetheless reported by `npm audit --omit=dev` as a direct HIGH, which is why an exception is needed at all rather than the finding simply not appearing.
exceptions.retires_when: The Prisma major upgrade lands. mysql2's only offered fix is a Prisma major, which touches the ORM for the entire clinical database and is scheduled under the clinical-DB bar rather than taken as a lockfile bump. This exception dies with that item.
